text:
Alex: Quick Q — customer hit a 500 and gave request_id=abc123. Console trace shows spans but the 'view logs' link is missing. Where's the canonical place to grab the raw request lines? Any quick checklist?
Maria: First thing — check ingest indexing lag. If logs haven't been indexed yet the console won't link. Run `curl -s https://observability.internal/ingest/status | jq .` and look at tailing delays.
Sam: Also confirm the trace has the x-request-id on a server span. Trace UI -> click the server span -> check attributes/tags. If the request id isn't propagated upstream the link won't exist.
Maria: Quick stern snippet I use for production proxy logs:```
stern -n production "api|edge" --container=proxy --since 10m | grep 'abc123'
``` That finds the pod emitting the header.
Alex: Nice, thanks. If I only have a trace_id (not request_id), what's the fastest map path?
Oliver: Search the trace by trace_id in Jaeger, open the root/server span and inspect span.attributes for request_id or x_request_ref. If the UI is missing fields you can run:```
observability trace get <trace_id> --json | jq -r '.spans[] | select(.kind=="server") | .attributes'
```
Sam: Another tip — the edge proxy (envoy) logs often include both trace_id and request_id in the same line, so grep for trace_id there. If console links are missing, edge->ingress logs are usually the bridge.
Ingester-bot: index-delay: 30s (info) :hourglass_flowing_sand:
Sam: If ingestion lag and trace attributes both fail, fallback is S3 raw log partition scan for the date prefix and `jq -c 'select(.request_id=="abc123")'` — slow but guarantees you don't miss late-arriving records.
Alex: Great, will try the ingest status then stern against proxy. Thanks all — I'll update thread if it's an ingest problem so we can tune the pipeline. :thumbsup:
